chunks: the First, so there is nothing before Him, and the Last, so there is nothing after Him, and the Manifest, so there is nothing above Him, and the Hidden, so there is nothing below Him.
ai.seo_question: What are the four divine attributes of Allah mentioned in the opening of Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited as part of the 'Supplication of the Eulogy' (Dua al-Tawassul) or general praises in Nahj al-Balagha, reflects the Shia theological emphasis on Allah's transcendence (tanzih) and immanence (tashbih) through the four key attributes: Al-Awwal, Al-Akhir, Al-Zahir, and Al-Batin. Sharif al-Radi’s compilation highlights these attributes to affirm God's absolute independence from creation while remaining intimately close to it, a concept deeply rooted in both Quranic exegesis and Shia hadith literature.

en.sayed-ali-raza: who is such First that nothing is before Him and such Last that there is nothing after him. He is such Manifest that there is nothing above Him and such Hidden that there is nothing nearer than He.
